Jatayu confronts Ravana mid-air knowing he cannot win; Source: Valmiki Ramayana (Aranya Kanda, Sarga 50-51); Lesson: Standing up against injustice is mandatory, even when defeat is guaranteed.

Sudama visits Dwarka with only crushed rice in torn cloth; Source: Srimad Bhagavatam (Skandha 10, Adhyaya 80-81); Lesson: True friendship and pure intent hold infinitely more value than lavish material offerings.

King Shibi offers his own flesh to save a frightened dove from a hawk; Source: Mahabharata (Vana Parva, Adhyaya 130-131); Lesson: Protecting those who seek refuge is the highest dharma, regardless of personal sacrifice.

Satyakama Jabala reveals his unknown lineage to Guru Gautama without shame; Source: Chhandogya Upanishad (Prapathaka 4, Khanda 4); Lesson: Truthfulness and honesty determine true nobility, not birth or caste.

Raja Harishchandra demands cremation tax from his own mourning queen at the ghat; Source: Markandeya Purana (Adhyaya 7-8); Lesson: Unwavering duty and commitment to truth must remain uncompromised even in extreme sorrow.

Bhasmasura tricks Lord Shiva for lethal power only to destroy himself through ego; Source: Bhagavata Purana (Skandha 10, Adhyaya 88); Lesson: Arrogance coupled with reckless power inevitably leads to self-destruction.
Maharishi Dadhichi donates his bones to forge Indra's Vajra; Source: Srimad Bhagavatam (Skandha 6, Adhyaya 10); Lesson: Supreme selflessness and sacrificing personal comfort for universal protection.
